title: Insert Interval
summary: Insert a new interval into a sorted list of disjoint intervals, merging wherever it overlaps.

tests.explain: [3, 4] overlaps nothing, so it goes into the gap between [1, 2] and [5, 8].
[5, 9] overlaps [4, 6] and [8, 10]. All three merge into [4, 10].
Inserting into an empty list leaves just the new interval.

hints: The list is already sorted and disjoint, so you don't need to sort. Think of three groups: intervals entirely before the new one, ones that overlap it, and ones entirely after it.
An interval is entirely before newInterval when its end < newInterval's start. Copy those as they are.
While intervals still overlap (start <= newInterval's end), grow newInterval to cover them with min/max. Push it, then copy everything that is left.

complexity.time: O(n): one pass over the list
